rule: judge_z + (BASE_CAP + (judge_z*probe_z > 0) * (MAX_CAP-BASE_CAP)) * PROBE_GAIN * probe_z, with judge_z replaced by big_margin/JUDGE_MARGIN_SD on the escalated disagreement rows
purpose: v4's gate with the disagreement branch handed to the tested model itself (27B/120B): on escalated rows the big judge replaces the cheap judge outright
derived_from: v4 (legacy_submissions/sonic_v4.ipynb); every v4 constant is unchanged

escalation.big_judge: the tested model itself, reusing the handle built for extraction
escalation.standardization: none -- big_margin goes over the same JUDGE_MARGIN_SD as the cheap judge; both are logit_1 - logit_0 on the same label tokens
escalation.batch_sizing: inherited from the probe config's extract_token_budget / extract_max_batch
escalation.substitution: full replacement of judge_z on the escalated rows; no blend weight
escalation.big_z: big_margin / JUDGE_MARGIN_SD -- the same divisor as the cheap judge. Not a calibration: JUDGE_MARGIN_SD is the 9B's margin spread, not the tested model's. See docs/sonic/sonic_v5.md section 4.
escalation.scope: all-or-nothing: every disagreement row, or none

selection.method: not fitted -- v5 adds no scoring constant
selection.why: the design replaces rather than nudges, so there is no cap to choose. A synthetic sweep (docs/sonic/sonic_v5.md section 10) shows a partial blend outscores full replacement at every big-judge quality level, turning positive only above ~0.85; a blend weight is the v5.1 lever if v5.0 underperforms.
selection.go_no_go: the big judge must beat the Phoenix 9B judge on dev rows with lora=None, on disagreement rows specifically; also compare the two margins' mean and spread there -- that is the group-placement risk in section 5

selection_notes.trigger_choice: v4.1 gated the cap on sigmoid(abs(probe_z)) and lost -0.0380 on Notus Nemotron: the probe is spuriously confident out of distribution, so no quantity derived from abs(probe_z) is a safe trigger
selection_notes.subset_standardization: NOT applied: big_margin substitutes as-is. The escalated rows are selected by detector conflict, so their label mix is skewed; if the big judge's margin runs hotter or colder than the cheap judge's, that group moves as a block in the dataset ranking. This is the design's largest untested assumption.
selection_notes.budget: NOTEBOOK_BUDGET is 1800s per (notebook, dataset) and the first SIGKILL aborts the whole submission. The escalation does not gate itself on the clock: measure its real cost on --dry.
